runbooks.diagnosis: LimeSurvey 6 only serves JSON-RPC when $config['RPCInterface'] = 'json' — the deployed default is 'off', yielding empty 200 responses. The patch must live INSIDE the returned 'config'=>array(...) block: top-level $config[...] assignments are discarded by the loader. config.php survives restarts but is lost on container recreate, and OPcache may serve stale bytecode after an edit.
remediation: Patch config.php: set 'RPCInterface' => 'json' inside the returned 'config'=>array(...) block
Restart the web process (clear OPcache) or restart the limesurvey container
Re-run a remotecontrol probe to confirm a non-empty response
Add the patch to the image build (Dockerfile) so recreates keep it

runbooks.diagnosis: On bad credentials LimeSurvey's controller die()s before emitting JSON — returning HTTP 200 text/html with an EMPTY body, indistinguishable from success to a naive client. A successful get_session_key returns a non-empty result with a 32-char session key.
remediation: Never report OK on an empty or non-JSON body
Treat an empty body after login as auth failure, not success
Verify the session key is non-empty (32 chars on success) before using it

runbooks.diagnosis: LimeSurvey's RPC handler returns an EMPTY body whenever the envelope id is falsy (0) — it treats id:0 as a notification. The positional-array login form (legacy XML-RPC) is also rejected by this build; login must use the object form {username, password} with a non-zero, monotonically increasing id.
remediation: Always send object-form params {username, password} (never positional arrays)
Send monotonically increasing envelope id values starting at 1 (++rpcId)
Apply to both the TS client and scripts/limesurvey-rpc.sh

runbooks.diagnosis: LimeSurvey rate-limits login attempts per client IP: wrong-password probes lock the client IP for ~10 minutes while the app itself is healthy — and since the lock is per IP, the internal container may be unaffected while an external script is locked, producing confusingly asymmetric behavior.
remediation: Wait out the lockout window (~10 min) before retrying
Avoid hammering wrong passwords; single-flight session-key caching (one auth per process)
If probing from behind NAT, account for the shared egress IP
